
  Every route asks the access policy for `events:read` or `events:write`
  first; src/adapters/http/access.rs explains the deny-by-default choice for the
  pages, src/adapters/http/api_access.rs for the JSON API under /v1/events.
  The JSON API at /v1/events takes the session cookie of the sign-in pages;
  changes send its CSRF token (the __Host-forge_csrf cookie) in X-CSRF-Token.
  Live updates: create, update and delete publish to the `events` channel of the tenant, and
  the index page subscribes; a stream is served only to callers the same policy
  grants `events:read` (src/adapters/http/streams.rs).
  Permissions match exactly: index and show need `events:read`, new, create,
  edit, update and delete need `events:write`, which the `owner` role has.
  Signed-out browsers are sent to /session/new (the sign-in pages of `forge new`
  or `forge generate authentication`); the pages use the tenant of the session.

  Then: forge migrate, and forge dev (or forge test).

declare src/domain/entities/mod.rs (pub mod event;)
//! Entities: domain objects with identity and invariants.

pub mod event;

declare src/application/ports/mod.rs (pub mod event_repository;)
//! Ports: traits implemented by adapters and infrastructure.

pub mod event_repository;

declare src/application/use_cases/mod.rs (pub mod events;)
//! Use cases: orchestration and transaction boundaries.

pub mod events;

declare src/infrastructure/database/mod.rs (pub mod events;)
//! PostgreSQL infrastructure: least-privilege tenant transaction setup.

pub mod events;

use forge::tenancy::TenantContext;
use sqlx::{PgPool, Postgres, Transaction};

/// Starts a PostgreSQL transaction and installs tenant/principal settings only
/// for that transaction.
///
/// RLS policies should read these values with current_setting(..., true). The
/// third set_config argument is true, so pooled connections do not retain tenant
/// identity after commit/rollback.
pub async fn begin_tenant_transaction<'a>(
    pool: &'a PgPool,
    context: &TenantContext,
) -> Result<Transaction<'a, Postgres>, sqlx::Error> {
    let mut transaction = pool.begin().await?;

    sqlx::query(
        "SELECT set_config('forge.tenant_id', $1, true), \
         set_config('forge.principal_id', $2, true)",
    )
    .bind(context.tenant_id().to_string())
    .bind(context.principal_id().to_string())
    .execute(&mut *transaction)
    .await?;

    Ok(transaction)
}

declare src/adapters/http/mod.rs (pub mod access; pub mod api_access; pub mod streams; pub mod events; pub mod events_api;)
//! HTTP adapter. Handlers stay thin: decode the request, call a use case and
//! map the result to a response, usually an HTML page rendered from a view
//! model in `views` (or a `303` redirect after a form submission).

pub mod access;
pub mod api_access;
pub mod authentication;
pub mod events;
pub mod events_api;
pub mod status;
pub mod streams;
pub mod views;

use std::sync::Arc;

use forge::ComposeError;
use forge::http::{Method, Request, Response, Router};
use forge::i18n::Translator;

use self::views::{Site, welcome::WelcomeIndex};

/// Whether the welcome page links to the sign-in pages.
const SIGN_IN: bool = true;

/// Loads the site and registers the digested assets and the request layers
/// every HTML page relies on (the request's locale, Content-Security-Policy,
/// CSRF protection with the `_method` override, flash messages). Every page
/// renders its layout from the returned site; `translator` is
/// `views::locales::translator(config)`.
pub fn site(router: &mut Router, translator: Translator) -> Result<Arc<Site>, ComposeError> {
    let site = Arc::new(Site::load(translator)?);
    site.register(router).map_err(ComposeError::other)?;
    Ok(site)
}

/// Registers the application's routes. Forge adds `/health`, `/health/live`
/// and `/health/ready` itself.
pub fn routes(router: &mut Router, site: &Arc<Site>) -> Result<(), ComposeError> {
    let index_site = Arc::clone(site);
    router.route(Method::GET, "/", move |request: Request| {
        let site = Arc::clone(&index_site);
        async move { index(&site, &request) }
    })?;
    status::routes(router)?;
    Ok(())
}

fn index(site: &Site, request: &Request) -> Response {
    forge::web::html(&WelcomeIndex {
        layout: site.layout(request),
        logo: site.logo(),
        application: env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME"),
        sign_in: SIGN_IN,
    })
}

declare src/adapters/http/views/mod.rs (pub mod events;)
//! Server-rendered views (ADR 0022). A view model is a plain struct checked
//! against its template in `templates/` at compile time by Askama; every
//! `{{ value }}` is HTML-escaped unless the template opts out with `|safe`.
//!
//! [`Site`] configures the asset pipeline (the counterpart of Rails'
//! `config/importmap.rb` and stylesheet tags) and the request's locale, and
//! [`Layout`] is what every page hands to `templates/layouts/application.html`.
//! Templates translate with `layout.i18n.t(KEY)` (see `locales`).

pub mod authentication;
pub mod events;
pub mod locales;
pub mod welcome;

use std::error::Error;
use std::sync::Arc;

use forge::http::{Request, Router};
use forge::i18n::Translator;
use forge::views::{
    AssetError, AssetSet, ContentSecurityPolicy, CsrfProtection, Flash, FlashLayer, I18n,
    ImportMap, LocaleNegotiation, csrf_meta, csrf_token, flash, vendor,
};

// `FORGE_ASSETS`: every file under assets/, digested and embedded by build.rs.
include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/forge_assets.rs"));

/// Digested assets, the import map, the Content-Security-Policy and the
/// translations shared by every page, built once at startup.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Site {
    translator: Arc<Translator>,
    assets: AssetSet,
    import_map: ImportMap,
    policy: ContentSecurityPolicy,
    stylesheet: String,
    javascript: String,
    logo: String,
}

impl Site {
    /// Validates the embedded assets (the application's and the vendored
    /// Turbo and Stimulus modules) and pins the JavaScript modules; pages
    /// are translated with `translator` (`locales::translator`).
    pub fn load(translator: Translator) -> Result<Self, Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>> {
        let assets = AssetSet::from_tables(&[FORGE_ASSETS, vendor::HOTWIRE_ASSETS])?;
        // Bare specifiers that `import` statements in assets/*.js may use.
        let import_map = ImportMap::builder()
            .pin("@hotwired/turbo", vendor::TURBO_ASSET)
            .pin("@hotwired/stimulus", vendor::STIMULUS_ASSET)
            .build(&assets)?;
        // Same-origin resources only; the import map is the one inline
        // script, allowed by its hash.
        let policy = ContentSecurityPolicy::strict().with_import_map(&import_map);
        let stylesheet = asset_path(&assets, "application.css")?;
        let javascript = asset_path(&assets, "application.js")?;
        let logo = asset_path(&assets, "forge-rust-logo.png")?;
        Ok(Self {
            translator: Arc::new(translator),
            assets,
            import_map,
            policy,
            stylesheet,
            javascript,
            logo,
        })
    }

    /// Digested URL of `assets/forge-rust-logo.png`, shown by the welcome page.
    pub fn logo(&self) -> &str {
        &self.logo
    }

    /// Registers one route per digested asset and the request layers, from
    /// the outermost: the request's locale (the `locale` cookie, then
    /// `Accept-Language`, then the default; translated responses get
    /// `Content-Language`), the Content-Security-Policy on every response,
    /// CSRF protection for every unsafe request (it also applies the
    /// `_method` override of HTML forms before routing) and flash messages.
    pub fn register(&self, router: &mut Router) -> Result<(), AssetError> {
        self.assets.register(router)?;
        router
            .layer(LocaleNegotiation::new(Arc::clone(&self.translator)))
            .layer(self.policy.clone())
            .layer(CsrfProtection::new())
            .layer(FlashLayer::new());
        Ok(())
    }

    /// The request's locale and the translator (`i18n.t(KEY).text()` in
    /// handlers). Without the locale layer, the default locale.
    pub fn i18n(&self, request: &Request) -> I18n {
        I18n::from_request(request).unwrap_or_else(|| self.default_i18n())
    }

    /// The default locale, for what is rendered without a request: live
    /// updates reach every subscriber in it (as Rails' broadcasts do).
    pub fn default_i18n(&self) -> I18n {
        I18n::new(
            Arc::clone(&self.translator),
            self.translator.default_locale(),
        )
    }

    /// The layout data of a page rendered for `request`. Reading it consumes
    /// the flash and issues the CSRF token the page's forms carry.
    pub fn layout(&self, request: &Request) -> Layout<'_> {
        Layout {
            i18n: self.i18n(request),
            csrf_meta: csrf_token(request).map(|token| csrf_meta(&token)),
            flash: flash(request),
            import_map: self.import_map.script_tag(),
            stylesheet: &self.stylesheet,
            javascript: &self.javascript,
        }
    }
}

fn asset_path(assets: &AssetSet, logical: &str) -> Result<String, Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>> {
    match assets.path(logical) {
        Some(path) => Ok(path.to_owned()),
        None => Err(format!("assets/{logical} is missing").into()),
    }
}

/// What `templates/layouts/application.html` renders around every page;
/// each page sets the document title in its `title` block.
pub struct Layout<'a> {
    /// The request's locale: `t`, `l`, `number` and `locale` in templates.
    pub i18n: I18n,
    /// `<meta name="csrf-token">` for Turbo and `fetch`. `None` only when
    /// CSRF protection is not installed, and then every form is refused.
    pub csrf_meta: Option<String>,
    /// The one-shot notice/alert set by the previous response.
    pub flash: Flash,
    /// The `<script type="importmap">` element (allowed by hash in the CSP).
    pub import_map: &'a str,
    /// Digested URL of `assets/application.css`.
    pub stylesheet: &'a str,
    /// Digested URL of `assets/application.js`.
    pub javascript: &'a str,
}

wire src/bootstrap/routes_gen.rs (scaffold events)
// forge:checksum c5b87706a65b14a89e34c9a2ef90db92350fb77495f9ac41cb198bd98f6417fe
//! Routes the generators mount. `forge generate scaffold`, `forge generate
//! resource` and `forge generate controller` write this file, and `forge
//! destroy` takes their blocks back out; each block starts with a `forge:`
//! comment. Do not edit it: the generators refuse to change it once its
//! checksum no longer matches. Mount your own routes in `compose`
//! (src/bootstrap/mod.rs), which calls this function once.

// A guard the application declares itself (a `fn protect` in
// src/bootstrap/mod.rs) replaces the generated one below, which the
// generators then leave out. Declaring one while the generated one is still
// here makes the name ambiguous, a compile error rather than a guard silently
// ignored: run the generator again.
#[allow(unused_imports)]
use super::*;
use guards::*;

/// Mounts the routes of the generated resources and controllers.
pub(super) fn generated_routes(
    composition: &mut forge::Composition<'_>,
    site: &std::sync::Arc<crate::adapters::http::views::Site>,
) -> Result<(), forge::ComposeError> {
    // forge:streams streams
    // Live updates (--broadcast), once for every broadcasting resource. On
    // PostgreSQL every replica hears every change (LISTEN/NOTIFY); production
    // needs FORGE_STREAMS_KEY (`openssl rand -base64 32`, the same everywhere).
    let streams =
        crate::adapters::http::streams::Streams::register(composition, forge::Fanout::Postgres)?;
    // forge:scaffold events
    {
        // events: tenant-scoped, at /events of the tenant the session signed in to,
        // for roles granted these permissions (the guard grants the owner role).
        let access = protect(
            composition,
            &[
                crate::application::use_cases::events::READ_PERMISSION,
                crate::application::use_cases::events::WRITE_PERMISSION,
            ],
        )?;
        let events = crate::application::use_cases::events::EventService::new(std::sync::Arc::new(
            crate::infrastructure::database::events::PgEventRepository::new(
                composition.postgres()?.clone(),
            ),
        ));
        crate::adapters::http::events::routes(
            composition.router(),
            site,
            events.clone(),
            access.clone(),
            &streams,
        )?;
        // events JSON API (/v1/events): the same session cookie and policy as the
        // pages; changes send the session's CSRF token in X-CSRF-Token.
        crate::adapters::http::events_api::routes(composition.router(), events, access)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The guards of the generated routes.
mod guards {
    // forge:guard protect
    /// The guard of tenant-scoped routes: sign-in, the CSRF token on changes, a
    /// membership in the session's tenant, and the `owner` role (`forge setup`)
    /// granted `permissions`. Declare `fn protect` with this signature in
    /// src/bootstrap/mod.rs to grant other roles; the generators then use yours.
    pub(super) fn protect(
        composition: &mut forge::Composition<'_>,
        permissions: &[&str],
    ) -> Result<
        std::sync::Arc<
            impl crate::adapters::http::access::TenantAccess
            + crate::adapters::http::api_access::ApiTenantAccess
            + 'static,
        >,
        forge::ComposeError,
    > {
        let mut policy = forge::security::RbacPolicy::new();
        let owner = forge::security::Role::new("owner").map_err(forge::ComposeError::other)?;
        for permission in permissions {
            let permission = forge::security::Permission::new(*permission)
                .map_err(forge::ComposeError::other)?;
            policy.allow(owner.clone(), permission);
        }
        let pool = composition.postgres()?.pool().clone();
        // Sessions end after FORGE_AUTH_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT without a request.
        let sessions = crate::infrastructure::auth::PostgresSessionStore::new(pool.clone())
            .with_idle_timeout(
                forge::auth::SessionIdleTimeout::new(
                    composition.config().auth.session_idle_timeout,
                )
                .map_err(forge::ComposeError::other)?,
            );
        Ok(std::sync::Arc::new(
            crate::adapters::http::access::SessionTenantAccess::new(
                std::sync::Arc::new(sessions),
                std::sync::Arc::new(crate::infrastructure::tenancy::PgMembershipStore::new(pool)),
                policy,
            ),
        ))
    }
}

  Every route asks the access policy for `posts:read` or `posts:write`
  first; src/adapters/http/access.rs explains the deny-by-default choice for the
  pages, src/adapters/http/api_access.rs for the JSON API under /v1/posts.
  Live updates: create, update and delete publish to the `posts` channel, and
  the index page subscribes; a stream is served only to callers the same policy
  grants `posts:read` (src/adapters/http/streams.rs).

  Then: forge migrate, and forge dev (or forge test).

wire src/bootstrap/routes_gen.rs (scaffold posts)
// forge:checksum 9088a3b7657ec3ccad881889fb10c669c49fc297dd583f002625e99610747ecd
//! Routes the generators mount. `forge generate scaffold`, `forge generate
//! resource` and `forge generate controller` write this file, and `forge
//! destroy` takes their blocks back out; each block starts with a `forge:`
//! comment. Do not edit it: the generators refuse to change it once its
//! checksum no longer matches. Mount your own routes in `compose`
//! (src/bootstrap/mod.rs), which calls this function once.

// A guard the application declares itself (a `fn protect` in
// src/bootstrap/mod.rs) replaces the generated one below, which the
// generators then leave out. Declaring one while the generated one is still
// here makes the name ambiguous, a compile error rather than a guard silently
// ignored: run the generator again.
#[allow(unused_imports)]
use super::*;
use guards::*;

/// Mounts the routes of the generated resources and controllers.
pub(super) fn generated_routes(
    composition: &mut forge::Composition<'_>,
    site: &std::sync::Arc<crate::adapters::http::views::Site>,
) -> Result<(), forge::ComposeError> {

    // Live updates (--broadcast), once for every broadcasting resource. On
    // PostgreSQL every replica hears every change (LISTEN/NOTIFY); production
    // needs FORGE_STREAMS_KEY (`openssl rand -base64 32`, the same everywhere).

        crate::adapters::http::streams::Streams::register(composition, forge::Fanout::Postgres)?;
    // forge:scaffold events
    {
        // events: tenant-scoped, at /events of the tenant the session signed in to,
        // for roles granted these permissions (the guard grants the owner role).
        let access = protect(
            composition,
            &[
                crate::application::use_cases::events::READ_PERMISSION,
                crate::application::use_cases::events::WRITE_PERMISSION,
            ],
        )?;
        let events = crate::application::use_cases::events::EventService::new(std::sync::Arc::new(
            crate::infrastructure::database::events::PgEventRepository::new(
                composition.postgres()?.clone(),
            ),
        ));
        crate::adapters::http::events::routes(
            composition.router(),
            site,
            events.clone(),
            access.clone(),
            &streams,
        )?;
        // events JSON API (/v1/events): the same session cookie and policy as the
        // pages; changes send the session's CSRF token in X-CSRF-Token.
        crate::adapters::http::events_api::routes(composition.router(), events, access)?;
    }
    // forge:scaffold posts
    {
        // posts: global. DenyAll refuses every request until you decide who may
        // use them: implement GlobalAccess (src/adapters/http/access.rs).
        let posts = crate::application::use_cases::posts::PostService::new(std::sync::Arc::new(
            crate::infrastructure::database::posts::PgPostRepository::new(
                composition.postgres()?.clone(),
            ),
        ));
        crate::adapters::http::posts::routes(
            composition.router(),
            site,
            posts.clone(),
            std::sync::Arc::new(crate::adapters::http::access::DenyAll),
            &streams,
        )?;
        // posts JSON API (/v1/posts): global. DenyAll refuses every request until
        // you decide who may use it: implement ApiGlobalAccess
        // (src/adapters/http/api_access.rs).
        crate::adapters::http::posts_api::routes(
            composition.router(),
            posts,
            std::sync::Arc::new(crate::adapters::http::api_access::DenyAll),
        )?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The guards of the generated routes.
mod guards {
    // forge:guard protect
    /// The guard of tenant-scoped routes: sign-in, the CSRF token on changes, a
    /// membership in the session's tenant, and the `owner` role (`forge setup`)
    /// granted `permissions`. Declare `fn protect` with this signature in
    /// src/bootstrap/mod.rs to grant other roles; the generators then use yours.
    pub(super) fn protect(
        composition: &mut forge::Composition<'_>,
        permissions: &[&str],
    ) -> Result<
        std::sync::Arc<
            impl crate::adapters::http::access::TenantAccess
            + crate::adapters::http::api_access::ApiTenantAccess
            + 'static,
        >,
        forge::ComposeError,
    > {
        let mut policy = forge::security::RbacPolicy::new();
        let owner = forge::security::Role::new("owner").map_err(forge::ComposeError::other)?;
        for permission in permissions {
            let permission = forge::security::Permission::new(*permission)
                .map_err(forge::ComposeError::other)?;
            policy.allow(owner.clone(), permission);
        }
        let pool = composition.postgres()?.pool().clone();
        // Sessions end after FORGE_AUTH_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT without a request.
        let sessions = crate::infrastructure::auth::PostgresSessionStore::new(pool.clone())
            .with_idle_timeout(
                forge::auth::SessionIdleTimeout::new(
                    composition.config().auth.session_idle_timeout,
                )
                .map_err(forge::ComposeError::other)?,
            );
        Ok(std::sync::Arc::new(
            crate::adapters::http::access::SessionTenantAccess::new(
                std::sync::Arc::new(sessions),
                std::sync::Arc::new(crate::infrastructure::tenancy::PgMembershipStore::new(pool)),
                policy,
            ),
        ))
    }
}
